findings.function: receiveFlashLoan, emergencyExit, withdrawAllToVault, withdrawToVault, doHardWork, salvage (SafeERC20 / Address inlined)
findings.source: Address.sol verifyCallResultFromTarget -> _revert(returndata, 'SafeERC20: low-level call failed'); SafeERC20 messages
findings.issue: 127 Error(string) reverts are built at the free pointer and printed as raw memory (the 63-digit 0x8c379a0... selector is most of the P6 count), although the same message is decoded as "revert with 'SafeERC20: low-level call failed'" at 1043 in the same function. Here the message length mem[_203] = 32 is lost after the call's return-data copy and the conditional 'mem[64] = ...' write.
findings.rule: Same root cause as P2: allocations at mem[64] only grow (each new mem[64] >= the previous one plus the allocated size), so a range allocated earlier ([_203, _203 + 64)) is disjoint from anything written later at or above the newer mem[64] (return-data copies, later allocations); forward its words across those writes, then fold the revert to "revert with 'message'".

findings.decompiled: s = 0 / while True: / if s >= stor4541: _20 = 0; break / if mem[32 * s + 172 len 20] != _token: s = s + 1; continue / _20 = 1; break / return bool(_20)
findings.source: BaseUpgradeableStrategyStorage.sol:119-124 for (uint i = 0; i < _list.length; i++) { if (_searchFor == _list[i]) return true; } return false;
findings.issue: The loop's own test is hidden as the first statement of 'while True', and both exits go through a flag; the getAddressArray loop just above also re-reads the invariant bound (_9 = stor4541) each iteration.
findings.rule: When the first statement of a 'while True' body is 'if c: <exit>', print 'while not c:' with the exit after the loop; an early 'return' from inside the body can stay a return instead of a flag and break. A bound re-assigned to the same invariant expression in every iteration is that expression.

notes: Long functions (doHardWork ~2,400 lines, withdrawToVault ~2,700, withdrawAllToVault ~1,600, emergencyExit ~800) reviewed by structure: loops, external calls (Aave POOL()/withdraw/repay/borrow, universal liquidator swaps, SafeERC20), storage writes and events; receiveFlashLoan, isRewardToken, rewardTokens() and the _liquidateReward loop checked in detail and correct (caller == Balancer vault 0xba12...c8, 'Only one can be true' / 'One has to be true', amounts[0] + fees[0] overflow check, makingFlashDeposit = stor3 branch, aToken() = address(stor8CDE)). Loop map: getAddressArray -> 'while s < _9' (rewardTokens(), isRewardToken and inlined copies), _isAddressInList -> 'while True' (isRewardToken), _liquidateReward -> 'while s < rewardTokens.length' (2902, 7924), _depositNoFlash -> 'while w < s' (6014, 9111), _redeemNoFlash -> 'while v > s' (5229, 6538, 9587) and, inlined with newBorrowTarget = 0, 'while u > 0' (1630, 4092). P7 counts the ABI encode loops of address[] ('mem[t] = Bytes(12, 0), mem[s + 12 len 20]') and receiveFlashLoan's calldata decode loop. Getter-named storage: aToken, debtToken etc. stay storNNNN because their getters return address(slot).
summary: Faithful, with every source loop a readable while; readability suffers mainly from 411 raw-memory call arguments (P2) and 127 Error(string) reverts left as memory writes, both from the unresolved free-memory pointer.
